items.title: A Borel reduction that eventually satisfies push-forward preserves Scott sentence complexity above a threshold
items.author: David Gonzalez; Dino Rossegger
items.work: Scott sentence complexities of linear orderings
items.difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author labelled proposition at source0.tex lines 696-704: if a Borel reduction Phi between the model classes of two vocabularies has Borel image and eventually satisfies push-forward, then above a threshold on the Scott rank the Scott sentence complexities of A and Phi(A) agree. The statement gives no bound and no construction, while the proof (source lines 706-718) has to manufacture one from three independent pieces of data: the measurability rank lambda of the reduction, the rank beta of a formula describing its image, and the rank delta from which the push-forward property starts to hold. It pushes a Scott sentence of A forward to one for Phi(A) by conjoining the pushed formula with the description of the image, pulls a Scott sentence of Phi(A) back with the pull-back theorem to get one for A of rank lambda plus epsilon, and then reads off the threshold at which the two bounds meet. The interaction of the three ranks is the whole content and it is invisible in the statement.
